deities: Chamunda Devi (fierce form of Durga/Kali - the presiding deity, worshipped as an ancient unearthed idol)
Shiva as Nandikeshwar (shrine in the complex, including a cave shrine with a Shiva Lingam under a boulder)
Hanuman and Bhairav (guardian deities flanking the sanctum)
festivals: Navratri (Chaitra and Sharad - the main festivals, drawing large crowds)
Aadi Himani Chamunda yatra (pilgrimage to the original hilltop shrine, feasible roughly May-June and October; route snowbound after mid-November)

history.dynasty: Katoch dynasty of Kangra (one source names Raja Umed Singh - single-source, verify)
history.summary: TOWN CORRECTION: CSV town 'Kangra' is wrong - the temple stands at Chamunda (Padar village) on the banks of the Baner (Ban Ganga) river, about 15 km from Dharamshala, 19 km from Palampur and 24-30 km from Kangra town. Dedicated to Chamunda - Kali's form after slaying the demons Chanda and Munda - with Shiva present as Nandikeshwar. The much older original shrine, Aadi Himani Chamunda, sits on a difficult hilltop; around 400 years ago a Kangra king and priest obtained the Devi's permission (she appeared in the priest's dream) to move worship to the accessible site, where an ancient buried idol of Chamunda was discovered and installed - the idol could reportedly be shifted only after the priest bathed and wore holy clothes, as others failed to displace it. IMPORTANT FLAG: widely called a Shakti Peetha in tourism and devotional literature, but Wikipedia (citing the Kalika Purana and Devi Bhagavata Purana) states it is NOT among the canonical 51/52 Shakti Peethas; it is counted among Himachal's five major Devi temples (with Chintpurni, Jwalamukhi, Brajeshwari and Naina Devi) on local pilgrimage-circuit tradition. Built in a Tantric-influenced style with murals from the Mahabharata, Ramayana and Devi Mahatmya; renovated after earthquake damage. The temple sits in a forested Dhauladhar setting beside the river.

name: Chamunda Devi Temple
town_description: Chamunda (Padar) is a pilgrimage village in Kangra district on the Baner river, on the Dharamshala-Palampur road (SH-17) about 15 km from Dharamshala, known for its Devi temple and as the base for the Aadi Himani Chamunda trek.
tradition: Hinduism (Shaktism; Shiva also worshipped as Nandikeshwar)

travel.airport: Kangra (Gaggal) Airport is the nearest airport (~30 km - verify).
travel.railway: Chamunda Marg is the nearest station on the narrow-gauge Kangra Valley Railway; Pathankot is the nearest broad-gauge railhead (~90 km).
travel.road: On the Dharamshala-Palampur road (SH-17); about 15 km from Dharamshala, 19 km from Palampur and 24-30 km from Kangra town. The Aadi Himani Chamunda shrine is a 9-13 km trek (5-7 hours one way) from here.

visitor_information.best_time: March to June and October to November; Navratri for the festival atmosphere (crowded). Avoid the Aadi Himani trek after mid-November due to snow.
visitor_information.opening_hours: About 6:00 AM to 7:00 PM daily (per triphobo.com); morning aarti around 6:15 AM (verify).
